6.1: An envelope says you are pre-approved, though a machine scanned your credit file.
6.2: A bank offers free checking and a sign-up bonus, then the fees activate a year later.
6.3: An advisor says "invest now and retire wealthy," then has moved firms by your retirement.
6.4: A bank you left sends a letter saying it wants you back, with a special rate.
6.5: After one late payment, a pre-approved person is reclassified high risk and charged more.
6.6: A customer calling about a fee is told it is in forty-seven pages of terms and conditions.
6.7: A worker who asks for a raise is labeled ungrateful, and one who accepts is underpaid.
6.8: The stock market works like a slot machine, random wins keeping you in through losses.
6.9: The credit score you needed last year is no longer enough this year.
6.10: Terms say "rates may vary" and "subject to change," a license to adjust after you commit.
6.11: A bank that charged hidden fees calls the customer irresponsible.
6.12: A customer who complains about hidden fees is told they should have read the contract.
6.13: A statement showing three hundred dollars in interest angers you, the twelfth does not.
6.14: Financial shame keeps people hiding debt from partners and struggles from friends.
6.15: A bank says another institution would charge more, though all lead to the same extraction.
6.16: Collection agencies you never borrowed from harass you over debts the lender gave up on.
6.17: A single financial crisis leaves a bad credit score that follows you for seven years.
6.18: An insurance claim is denied with no explanation, and calls loop through menus.
6.19: You sign loan documents at peak emotional investment, formatted to discourage reading.
6.20: A worker says "I can't leave this job, I need the benefits," bonded to their employer.
6.21: A person denied loans and buried in debt eventually stops trying to build stability.
6.22: An advisor says "let me handle this for you, it's too complex for most people."

6.24: The first question at every gathering is "what do you do," so net worth is self-worth.

6.29: A new borrower fills your slot the next business day on identical terms.

9.28: A person released from prison walks out with a bus ticket, a box of belongings, no plan.

30.1: The Statue of Liberty welcomes "your tired, your poor" while the border says otherwise.
30.2: A refugee gets ninety days of support, then is released into a society they do not know.
30.3: An applicant told "your case will be processed" waits years in limbo.
30.4: A deported person who returns is detained and processed again, generating the per diem.
30.5: A doctor drives a taxi, an engineer washes dishes and a professor cleans offices.
30.6: An immigrant mistreated over an accent is told "that's not what happened."
30.7: An immigrant must assimilate and lose their identity or keep it and not belong.
30.8: The visa lottery grants residency to a small percentage and keeps millions hoping.

30.10: An applicant is told "your application is under review," with no timeline or criteria.
30.11: A nation that displaced immigrants asks "why don't they fix their own country?"
30.12: An immigrant who reports workplace exploitation is threatened with deportation.
30.13: By the thousandth "where are you really from?" the sting is replaced by a practiced smile.
30.14: An immigrant is alone in a city they don't understand, navigating systems they can't read.
30.15: Citizens are told "they're competing for your job" and "they're using your resources."
30.16: A "good immigrant" performs gratitude and distance from the "bad immigrant."
30.17: An immigrant is told "they don't learn the language" though no free classes exist.

30.19: An immigrant accepts a visa that ties their legal existence to the employer's sponsorship.

30.21: A person in immigration limbo for years learns the system does not respond to effort.
30.22: An employer who sponsored an H-1B worker controls their right to remain in the country.
30.23: An immigrant faces forms in a language they don't speak and hearings without translation.
